title: Reused places across a simulation schedule
mode: built-in image_gen tool; new image generation
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: finished editorial cover for a scholarly physics and technology review, wide 16:9 landscape, high resolution.
Primary request: Make a beautiful, scientifically disciplined conceptual artwork about the SAME storage place being used, released after measurement, and then used again at a later time. This temporal reuse is the one main event. It illustrates a classical state-vector simulation schedule, not a physical quantum computer and not data.
Scene and subject: An elegant sculptural paper construction on a warm ivory ground. Three thin translucent vellum sheets are suspended in a shallow, gently oblique exploded view, staggered from rear-left to front-right as successive time stages. Each sheet has the same sparse orderly array of architectural rectangular bays, precisely aligned with faint graphite registration guides across time. Focus on ONE corresponding central bay repeated across the three layers: on the rear-left sheet a small sculptural vermilion folded-paper loop occupies that bay; on the middle sheet that very bay is conspicuously empty, a clean luminous vacancy with its contour still visible; on the front-right sheet the same bay is occupied anew by a differently folded vermilion loop. The middle vacancy must be visually unmistakable and remain unobstructed. Other sparse graphite elements quietly retain their places. A few tiny discrete graphite stitch marks leave the first stage and continue along a fine line outside the bays toward the right, a subtle metaphor for persisting classical measurement records; do not draw a duplicate of the loop along this record line.
Style and medium: Original sophisticated editorial paper collage and fine dry graphite drawing, tactile archival paper fibers, careful cut edges, translucent overlays, restrained geometric precision, deep artistic judgment, subtle imperfect handmade texture. Contemporary museum print quality. No imitation of a named artist or publication.
Composition: One calm unified sculptural scene, not a three-panel infographic. Wide 16:9 framing, generous clean negative space, strong single focal progression occupied-empty-reoccupied. Large simple forms readable at thumbnail size. The sheets share one consistent perspective and one consistent set of bay registrations. Reuse through time must be clearer than any decorative complexity.
Lighting and palette: Diffuse raking daylight, delicate graphite shadows, warm ivory and pale grey paper with a very small but deliberate cinnabar/vermilion accent. A quiet, analytical and poetic atmosphere.
Text: None.
Scientific invariants: The vacant middle bay represents released storage ONLY AFTER a measurement, not squeezing or copying an unknown quantum state. The artwork must not imply arbitrary compression of a 104-qubit state into 45 qubits. The array sizes and folds have no quantitative meaning. This is a temporal conceptual metaphor, not a simulation plot, not an exact circuit, and not a device rendering.
Avoid: Text, letters, numerals, labels, arrows, equations, chart axes, logos, watermark, exact qubit counts, binary code, circuit-board motifs, blue or neon glow, server racks, cryostats, stars, planets, brains, robots, many objects funneling into a smaller box, mystical entanglement clouds, metallic science-fiction gloss. Do not show objects being compressed. No people.

caption_ko: 반투명한 종이층은 시간 순서를, 주홍색 접힘과 가운데 빈자리는 측정·해제 뒤 같은 저장공간을 다시 쓰는 과정을 상징한다. 가는 점의 흔적은 남아 있는 고전 측정 기록을 뜻한다. 실제 회로·큐비트 수·계산 데이터가 아닌 AI 생성 개념 일러스트.
caption_en: Translucent paper layers represent successive times; the vermilion folds and intervening vacancy symbolize storage being released after measurement and reused later. Fine dotted traces stand for retained classical measurement records. AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an exact circuit, qubit count, or simulation data.
alt_ko: 나란히 정렬된 세 종이 격자의 같은 자리에 주홍색 접힘, 밝은 빈칸, 새로운 주홍색 접힘이 차례로 나타나고 가는 흑연 점의 기록이 옆으로 이어진다.
alt_en: Three aligned paper lattices show a vermilion fold, a bright empty bay, and a new fold in the same place across time, with a fine graphite record continuing beside them.

visual_qa.primary_event: Pass: occupied central bay → conspicuous empty corresponding bay → reoccupied corresponding bay.
visual_qa.geometry: Pass for conceptual correspondence: repeated lattice bays align across successive sheets; no circuit topology is claimed.
visual_qa.misleading_compression: Pass: no funnel, shrinking box, or accumulation of many states into one smaller state.
visual_qa.style: Pass: warm paper, graphite line, restrained vermilion, coherent soft light; no blue-neon server or generic quantum decoration.
visual_qa.text_and_logos: Pass: no visible text, equations, numerals, or branding.
visual_qa.thumbnail_320x180: Pass after viewing actual 320 × 180 derivative: the two occupied bays remain strong focal points, and the lighter intervening empty bay remains discernible. Fine record marks are secondary at this size.
visual_qa.grayscale_320x180: Pass after viewing actual grayscale derivative: dark occupied forms and the intervening bright vacancy remain distinguishable without hue.
limitations: A caption is required to establish that layers represent time and the thin dotted line represents classical records.
The illustration cannot establish which precise physical position is measured, released, or allocated in the actual protocol.
The folds are symbolic storage occupancy, not a depiction of a quantum wavefunction or a physical qubit.
